summary: A short 1969 note by Vint Cerf about a message of zero text length used to signal end-of-file. It shows a message layout containing a leader, a marking field, a checksum and padding. It is an early, informal protocol note.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 13 proposes marking the end of a file by sending a message with no text. Its figure shows that the message still has a leader, marking, checksum and padding.

subtitle: A proposal to use a zero-text-length message to mark the end of a file.

tldr.problem: File transmissions over auxiliary connections need a way to indicate that no more file data follows.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 13 proposes a message with zero text length and shows a leader, marking, checksum and padding in its format.
tldr.outcome: The one-page note proposes an end-of-file signal but does not specify receiver behavior.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 13 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text is a brief proposal dated 20 August 1969.

sections.title: A Signal for the End of a File
sections.content:
The note refers to RFC 11 and says that file transmissions over auxiliary connections need a way to specify END-OF-FILE. Vint Cerf proposes using a message whose length is zero for this purpose.

The note presents this as a proposal and gives a diagram of the message format.
sections.plainLanguage: A file transfer needs a clear way to say that no more text is coming. The proposal uses a message with zero text length as that signal.

sections.title: Format of the Empty Message
sections.content:
The figure shows a 32-bit leader, a 32-bit marking, a 16-bit checksum and a padding field whose width is shown as unknown. The text length is zero, but the message still contains these other fields.

The document does not define what the fields mean or give a fixed padding size.
sections.plainLanguage: The message carries no text, but it still has other fields, including a checksum. The figure does not state how wide the padding field is.

sections.title: What the Proposal Leaves Unspecified
sections.content: RFC 13 is a one-page proposal that refers to RFC 11 for the context of auxiliary-connection file transfers. It does not explain how a receiver should react to the zero-length message or describe error handling.
sections.plainLanguage: The note suggests the signal and shows its layout. It does not say what the receiving computer should do next.
